display.title: Episode 513: The King Is Watching (Parshas Mishpatim)
display.summary_short: For Parshas Mishpatim, Uncle Yossi explains the Shulchan Aruch and its first rule, 'Shivisi Hashem', then tells how a rabbi stopped a hungry coachman from stealing the king's apples.
display.summary_long: Broadcast the week of Parshas Mishpatim. Uncle Yossi explains that Hashem told Moshe Rabbeinu to set out the laws 'before them' like a table ready to eat from, which is why the code of Jewish law is called the Shulchan Aruch, the set table. Every Jewish home should have one, and its first line is from Tehillim: 'Shivisi Hashem lenegdi samid', I set Hashem before me always. Remembering that Hashem is always with us makes us careful in thought, speech and action, and joyful too. After the Hakochainik march, a student from Beis Rivkah says the Shema and everyone gives tzedakah. Story time: a hungry coachman driving old Rabbi Yitzchak stops at the king's orchard to take apples. The rabbi agrees to keep watch and soon cries out, 'He's watching!' The frightened coachman flees, then learns that the rabbi meant the King of all kings, who forbade stealing. He resolves never to steal again. The show ends with Shabbos Mevarchim Adar, the call to increase in joy, and candle-lighting times.
display.lesson: Hashem is always watching, so be honest in everything you do, even when no one else can see.
